# Chief engineer advice: preserve the complete dispatch commit scope

Recommendation: **adjust**. Add one fail-closed check for the complete task commit scope before the wrapper writes anything, then exercise that boundary through the real builder. Checking only the reused record's index would leave the same loss mechanism reachable through other task files.

```yaml
chief_engineer_advice:
  outcome: A Pilot stage dispatch records its actual inputs in the stamp commit without consuming or destroying pre-existing task work.
  next_step: Add a shared clean-task-scope precondition before select_record, covering fresh dispatch, retry and advance; prove preservation with the real pinned builder and scoped state comparisons.
  material_risk: Another writer can change a scoped file or index entry after a one-time check; the proposed check is not a transaction lock.
  decision_needed: FO owns routing the repair and ensuring exclusive same-task writes during dispatch; no new Captain decision is needed within that boundary.
  defer:
    - Upstream Spacedock changes or a general multi-writer transaction system, unless exclusive same-task writes cannot be established.
    - Model and roster derivation, separate version preflights, and automatic follow-up records, as already excluded.
  recommendation: adjust
```

## Evidence and route

Read at product head `0d84d5d1b96fd674dba3a442d69c2e7898cceccd`, branch `spacedock-ensign/dispatch-build-writes-the-dispatch-record`, in `/Users/kent/conductor/workspaces/kc-claude-plugins/colombo/.context/dev2-adoption/worktree/.worktrees/spacedock-ensign-dispatch-build-writes-the-dispatch-record`; its working tree was clean. Assigned base: `334d91e3165953b2ca7191e3308d80b6c02c4a99`. Workflow checkout remains `ba055b8a7a55a787ac989c4cef52d07dd75661ad`. Task state is `validation`, profile `pilot` (bounded real use).

The accepted task design and architecture decision record (ADR) 0070 retain the package wrapper and Spacedock's existing commit seam. ADR 0027 places structured checks at the write; ADRs 0014, 0037 and 0048 retain separate preflights, work ownership and First Officer (FO) publication authority. This advice changes repair sequencing within those boundaries; it grants no gate, validation, merge or release approval.

At `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/dispatch_stage.py:46–54`, identical retry returns before the new-path index check; exclusive creation protects only a new record. At lines 58–65, cleanup removes an invocation-created record and its index entry if absent from HEAD. Neither protects other paths the builder stages. The supplied `validation-2/retry-index-probe.json` shows success with a changed index blob, unchanged working bytes and unchanged HEAD; the refusal control preserves all three. I inspected these artifacts, not reran the probe.

The validator's retained Spacedock 0.27.2 source, `/tmp/pr812-validation2.gfsHcD/spacedock-4d158a484ec73e184861067f8ed1e20087fdc26a`, confirms the broader boundary: `internal/dispatch/stamp.go:247–264` runs path-scoped `git add -A` before commit; `entityCommitPaths` at lines 322–335 includes the flat task file plus its companion directory, or the entire folder-form task directory. Inline stamping uses the same pattern at lines 217–235. Advance's later state commit also stages its entity unit (`internal/cli/state_sync.go:359–433`). Thus a staged-only edit to the task file, an older dispatch or a review/report file can encounter the same mechanism. That broader reach is a source inference, not a newly executed reproduction.

## One precondition before any write

Require **the entire resolved commit scope to be clean against HEAD in both the index and worktree**, with no pre-existing untracked content that the stamp would add. Define the scope from the builder's entity unit, including the companion directory that record creation will introduce; do not reduce it to the chosen record or `dispatch/`.

- For every tracked path in that scope, HEAD, the index and the worktree must agree in content, existence and Git-relevant type/mode. Refuse staged changes, unstaged changes, staged-only changes with worktree restored to HEAD, partial staging, additions, deletions, renames and unresolved index entries. Even equal staged/worktree edits differing from HEAD are refused: they are pre-existing work, not owned by this dispatch.
- For paths absent from HEAD, refuse existing index entries or nonignored untracked files in the scope. Independently require the selected new record path to be absent, retaining exclusive creation; ignored files or dangling symlinks must not let that path be overwritten. Reuse is allowed only after the scope passes, and still requires the current adding-commit and expected-input rules.
- Resolve the actual state repository and canonical task layout; use literal, NUL-safe path handling. Inspect both comparisons (index versus HEAD and worktree versus index), plus untracked paths. A command failure or unresolved scope is a hold, not an empty result. Do not rely solely on a status shortcut that can hide `assume-unchanged` or `skip-worktree` entries: verify their content explicitly or refuse those scoped entries. Refuse an unsupported path escape/type instead of declaring it clean.

Call this once after read-only argument/scope resolution and **before `select_record`**, including its directory creation, so fresh, reused, changed-input and `--advance` paths all pass it. On refusal, name the path and staged/unstaged condition, return nonzero with `dispatch_stage: dispatch not built;`, emit no envelope and invoke neither builder nor cleanup. Preserve the existing ownership restriction on cleanup; do not add automatic reset, stash or commit as a remedy.

Why this closes the pre-existing-state class: every admitted pre-existing scoped version is already represented by HEAD, and there is no additional staged or worktree version for staging to replace. The wrapper then creates only its own record before the builder's authorized task mutation. This is deliberately more conservative than allowing any state where index happens to equal worktree.

**Concurrency limit:** no check performed only once can guarantee preservation against a writer acting after it. Exclusive same-task ownership must last through build/commit/cleanup. Git's transient `index.lock` retry in `stamp.go:353–371` does not provide that ownership across the sequence. If FO cannot establish it, hold and return that concrete constraint for an isolated state checkout or coordinated upstream transaction design; another record-specific condition cannot solve it.

## Cost to normal use

A clean task and clean immediate retry keep the same invocation and numbering. Local Git reads add unmeasured latency and no network request. Pending edits anywhere in this task now hold dispatch, even when they could safely have been committed together; FO must have their owner preserve/reconcile and intentionally commit them first. In particular, blindly running `state commit` on divergent staged/worktree content would repeat the loss and is not a safe recovery instruction. Do not require unrelated tasks or the whole code checkout to be clean. Explain the remedy in the refusal diagnostic; no new workflow gate or word-budget increase is needed.

## Proof required for the next repair

Extend the existing real-binary suite with a table-driven preservation matrix; retain the accepted success and failure tests.

1. **Locations and routes:** apply dirty-state cases to the new record path, reused committed record, older dispatch, task frontmatter and nested companion report. Exercise flat and folder-form tasks, fresh dispatch, immediate retry, new round and advance. A clean selected record with a dirty sibling must hold.
2. **States:** cover index-only change, worktree-only change, index/worktree equal but different from HEAD, index/worktree each different, and the reported worktree-equals-HEAD case. Include untracked files, staged additions with/without a worktree file, staged/unstaged deletions, renames across the scope boundary, conflicts and type/mode changes. Cover the special flags and literal-path cases used by the implementation. This derives cases from the three representations, rather than adding only another retry fixture.
3. **Refusal oracle:** snapshot HEAD, all scoped file bytes/existence/modes, semantic index entries (blob, mode, stage and relevant flags), and outside-scope sentinel state. Assert nonzero, named diagnostic, empty stdout, no builder call, no new record or frontmatter change, and preservation of every snapshot. Run dirty cases with otherwise valid inputs so refusal cannot be credited to the record checker.
4. **Allowed and recovery paths:** real 0.27.2 builder commits matching inputs from a clean scope; immediate retry reuses; changed inputs or a later commit mint the next number; advance commits before its envelope. Unrelated staged and unstaged task work stays intact and outside the dispatch commit. An owner-reconciled/committed task becomes dispatchable. Checker failure, staged-then-failed build, and committed-then-assembly failure retain the existing cleanup/retry contracts.
5. **Falsifiers and integration:** remove the guard; omit the index comparison; omit worktree/untracked inspection; narrow scope to the selected record or dispatch directory; place the guard after record creation; bypass it on retry or advance. Each mutant must fail the matching preservation assertion. Run the unchanged acceptance chain plus these cases on the new exact head, then obtain the existing hosted real-binary check. Use a controlled overlapping-writer probe to establish any concurrency claim; otherwise retain the exclusive-writer limitation explicitly.

## Unverified and handoff

This is read-only engineering advice, not independent validation of a repair. I ran no tests or Git writes and changed only this report. I inspected the named task, repair dispatch, evidence, candidate source/tests and retained upstream source; I did not independently refetch that source or refresh GitHub review/CI state. The latest supplied validation records hosted acceptance criterion 8 as unmet after an HTTP 504 download failure; that is missing hosted evidence, not a proven product defect. CI cost per PR remains unmeasured; keep existing narrow triggers. Current worker execution, concurrent-writer safety, post-release adoption and delivery remain unverified. FO owns repair dispatch, exact-head revalidation, hosted evidence and committing this report.

content.content:
# Pilot: bounded real use

Deliver one integrated user journey for limited real use and likely iteration,
without silently accepting long-term production obligations.
Use repository-native structure where it lowers near-term iteration cost;
avoid hypothetical scale and general-purpose platform work.

Cover real persistence and external seams. Include diagnostics, recovery,
duplicate handling and data safety where the accepted journey exposes them.
Test owned behavior and real seams rather than stable vendor internals.

Return to profile selection if scope adds production data or credentials, broad
exposure, a consumer-required compatibility migration, irreversible migration,
unattended recurring operation, support/SLO duty or release/rollback ownership.
A normal published upgrade that consumers can absorb remains eligible for Pilot
with its applicable version and migration-note obligations; publication alone
does not select Production.
# Validation principles

Check the exact delivered artifact against the approved outcome and relevant
primary evidence. Separate checks actually run, evidence only read, and work
not verified. Observe the selected failure boundary as well as the successful
path when that boundary determines acceptance. At the same candidate, assess both
goal sufficiency and minimal necessity: does the accepted goal work at the selected
profile's depth, and does the without-it observation justify each retained change
or removal? Check that remaining surfaces map to the goal, a named falsifier,
safety boundary or required lifecycle obligation; a deletion earns its place by
the same standard as retention. Use existing evidence, not a new proof harness.

Read every comment the candidate adds. A comment that narrates the change, restates
the code beside it, cites a line number or marks a section is a repair finding.
Measure them with
`python3 <package>/scripts/comment_ratio.py <base> <candidate> --workflow-dir <workflow-dir>`
and report its output. Exit 1 (a ratio above the maximum, or a comment citing task
numbering, review provenance, a PR or issue number or a `file:line`) is a repair
finding returned through feedback; exit 2 is a configuration error that returns to FO.
The citation scan finds the named classes only, so still read every added comment.
When the task has a `## Number guards` section, rerun its `check` at the candidate; exit 1 is a repair
finding returned through feedback and exit 2 is a configuration error that returns to FO.
Validation runs `python3 <package>/scripts/adr_lint.py docs/adr --since <base>`, which
requires every record the candidate added or changed, plus `--require <numbers>` for
each `ADR:` number the task's `## Number guards` reserves and any number the
implementation report names; exit 1 or a missing record returns through the existing
feedback route, and exit 2 is a configuration error that returns to FO.
Read the task's dispatch records (`<task>/dispatch/` in the state checkout) for the
implementation cycles you validate, and run
`python3 <package>/scripts/dispatch_records.py <task folder>`; a missing or incomplete
record (its exit 1), or a requirement in it that traces to no accepted criterion or
Captain ruling, is a finding for FO.
When the change alters what a user sees, the evidence includes a screenshot of the
changed screen at the candidate; reading the code or a passing render test is not
seeing it.
When the task's `Surfaces:` include `ui` and it has a `Design review:` line, dispatch
`kc-dev-flow-2:design-director` with that screenshot (pass 2a: `Screenshots:`,
`Criteria:` naming the criteria whose text names the running screen, `ADR folder:` as
in [design-review.md](../ideation/design-review.md)). Give `Screenshots:` as the path relative to the task folder (for example
`design/built-1.png`) and add `Task folder:` with its absolute path so the director can open it;
the report's `preview:` copies that relative path, which is the form the check resolves and
the only one it accepts. Save its report as
`design/validation-<N>.yaml` and write `Built screen review: design/validation-<N>.yaml`
in your validation Stage Report (the check reads the last one) with one `Built screen finding <n>:` line per finding: `F<N>` for a MAJOR, naming
its bullet in your report, and `declined: <reason>` or `Needs decision: <text>` for a
MINOR. Send each MINOR you would decline to the director first (pass 2b), save the
rulings as `design/validation-declines-<N>.yaml` and name them on a
`Built screen decline check:` line; a decline it overrules or sends to a decision
becomes `Needs decision:`. Only the Captain's quoted words waive the review:
`Built screen review: waived 「<his words>」`.

For a decisive check, identify evidence that it detects the relevant known error.
Reuse applicable negative or mutation evidence; only when it is missing, run the
smallest counterexample needed. Do not rerun every check or an already-green suite
just to demonstrate this principle.

Every validation stage ends with a minimal acceptance script the Captain can run
himself: three to six steps, five minutes or less, each naming the action and the
expected observation, written for someone outside this session — an exact command
or URL, no internal identifier to look up, no secret in the text. FO runs it as
written before the gate, so it runs unchanged in a fresh shell and names any checkout
or install it needs. State what it
does not cover, so a pass is not mistaken for proof of the whole change. When the
change has no user-visible surface, the script says so and substitutes the
smallest observable command whose output he can read, rather than being
omitted silently.

Report verdict, artifact identity, evidence and material limits in the existing
SD stage report. List each finding as its own `- F<N> <Class>: …` bullet, and split a
finding with parts into one bullet per part. A code repair returns through implementation feedback; scope or
profile changes return to the affected user decision. The user or named owner
retains gate and delivery authority. Green checks do not prove merge or adoption.
Do not invoke local fallback, push the trunk, merge, or clean up an owned worktree unless
the specific action is authorized.
# Pilot validation

Verify the accepted limited-use journey across its real seams and selected
failure/recovery conditions. Distinguish missing evidence from a demonstrated
defect. Check applicable consumer-visible delivery notes at the exact revision.
Return new production obligations to the user rather than accepting them under
Pilot by implication.
# Retained documents

Read only when the task changes retained documentation or behavior already
described there. Use the project's existing authoritative context; do not require
a new architecture file or a repository-wide documentation sweep.

Keep a correct structure and update the affected claims with the approved change.
Give each mutable fact one authoritative home and link to it; leave in-progress
status in the existing task. Before removing affected sections or files, locate
where their necessary content remains and preserve anything uniquely needed.
Do not delete unrelated content merely to simplify this change.

Check the reader's entry path and affected claims against the actual result.
For affected diagrams, render them and compare actors, order, branches and
approval boundaries with the prose and implementation where applicable. A
successful render proves syntax/presentation, not semantic agreement. Report any
unverified rendering or claim as a limit, not a passed check.

  8 │ import re
  9 │ import stat

 14 │ from number_guards import Misconfigured, frontmatter
 15 │ 
 16 │ SCRIPTS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
 17 │ 
 18 │ 
 19 │ def git(root, *args):
 20 │     return subprocess.run(["git", "--literal-pathspecs", "-C", str(root), *args], check=True,
 21 │                           capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
 22 │ 
 23 │ 
 24 │ def resolve_scope(args):
 25 │     value = frontmatter(args.workflow_dir / "README.md").get("state", "")
 26 │     relative = Path(value)
 27 │     if relative.is_absolute() or ".." in relative.parts:
 28 │         raise ValueError(f"{str(args.workflow_dir / 'README.md')!r}: unsupported state path")
 29 │     container = args.workflow_dir if value in ("", "$inline") else args.workflow_dir / relative
 30 │     if container.resolve(strict=True) != container:
 31 │         raise ValueError(f"{str(container)!r}: symlinked state directory")
 32 │     state = Path(git(container, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel")).resolve(strict=True)
 33 │     if not container.is_relative_to(state) or (value not in ("", "$inline") and state != container):
 34 │         raise ValueError(f"{str(container)!r}: unsupported state repository layout")
 35 │     entity = args.entity_path
 36 │     folder = task_folder(entity)
 37 │     if (args.entity_input != entity or entity.suffix != ".md"
 38 │             or (entity.parent.parent if entity.name == "index.md" else entity.parent) != container):
 39 │         raise ValueError(f"{str(args.entity_input)!r}: unsupported or symlinked task layout")
 40 │     for directory in (folder, folder / "dispatch"):
 41 │         if os.path.lexists(directory) and (directory.is_symlink() or not directory.is_dir()):
 42 │             raise ValueError(f"{str(directory)!r}: unsupported task directory type")
 43 │     scope = [folder] if entity.name == "index.md" else [entity, folder]

self.assert_existing_record_is_preserved(staged=True, missing=True)

    def scope_seed(self, layout="flat", route="fresh"):
        self.env["GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS"] = "0"
        if layout == "folder":
            self.folder.mkdir()
            destination = self.folder / "index.md"
            self.git(self.state, "mv", "--", self.entity, destination)
            self.entity = destination
            self.commit_task()
        self.older = self.folder / "dispatch/validation-1.md"
        self.older.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.older.write_text(f"# validation-1\nDispatched: {'a' * 40}\nModel: fixture\nCandidate: {'a' * 40}\n"
                              f"\n## Checklist\nInspect the previous artifact.\n\n## Scope notes\n{self.notes.read_text()}")
        self.report = self.folder / "review/nested/report.md"
        self.report.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
        self.report.write_text("Original companion report.\n")
        self.literal = self.folder / "review/[literal] space\nreport.md"
        self.literal.write_text("Literal path report.\n")
        self.outside = self.state / "other-task.txt"
        self.outside.write_text("Outside HEAD bytes.\n")
        (self.state / "rename-source.txt").write_text("Outside rename source.\n")
        self.git(self.state, "add", "--", self.folder, self.outside, self.state / "rename-source.txt")
        self.git(self.state, "commit", "-m", "test: clean task scope")
        stage, extra = "ideation", ()
        if route == "advance":
            self.set_stage("implementation")
            self.build("implementation")
            stage, extra = "implementation", ("--advance",)
        elif route in ("retry", "new-round"):
            self.build()
            if route == "new-round":
                history = self.state / "outside-history.txt"
                history.write_text("An unrelated state commit.\n")
                self.git(self.state, "add", "--", history)
                self.git(self.state, "commit", "-m", "test: outside history")
        return stage, extra

    def scope_snapshot(self):
        files = {}
        for root in (self.state, *getattr(self, "extra_roots", [])):
            paths = [root]
            if root.is_dir() and not root.is_symlink():
                for parent, directories, names in os.walk(root, followlinks=False):
                    directories[:] = [name for name in directories if name != ".git"]
                    paths += [Path(parent) / name for name in directories + names if name != ".git"]
            for path in paths:
                info = path.lstat()
                value = [stat.S_IFMT(info.st_mode), stat.S_IMODE(info.st_mode)]
                value.append(os.readlink(path) if path.is_symlink() else path.read_bytes().hex() if path.is_file() else None)
                files[str(path)] = value
        return dict(head=self.git(self.state, "rev-parse", "HEAD"), files=files,
                    index=self.call(["git", "-C", self.state, "ls-files", "--stage", "--debug", "-z"]).stdout,
                    flags=self.call(["git", "-C", self.state, "ls-files", "-v", "-z"]).stdout)

    def dirty_outside(self):
        self.outside.write_text("Outside staged bytes.\n")
        self.git(self.state, "add", "--", self.outside)
        self.outside.write_text("Outside working bytes, different again.\n")
        (self.state / "untracked-other-task.txt").write_text("Outside untracked bytes.\n")

    def scope_dirty(self, path, change):
        original = path.read_bytes() if path.exists() else b"Prepared record.\n"
        edited = original + b"A preserved edit.\n"
        if change in ("staged-only", "equal-change", "partial"):
            path.write_bytes(edited)
            self.git(self.state, "add", "--", path)
            if change != "equal-change":
                path.write_bytes(original if change == "staged-only" else edited + b"Working-only edit.\n")
        elif change in ("worktree-only", "literal"):
            path.write_bytes(edited)
        elif change in ("untracked", "staged-add", "staged-add-missing", "intent-to-add", "ignored-existing"):
            path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            path.write_bytes(edited)
            if change in ("staged-add", "staged-add-missing", "intent-to-add"):
                self.git(self.state, "add", *("-N",) if change == "intent-to-add" else (), "--", path)
            if change == "staged-add-missing":
                path.unlink()
        elif change == "staged-delete":
            self.git(self.state, "rm", "--cached", "--", path)
        elif change == "unstaged-delete":
            path.unlink()
        elif change == "both-delete":
            self.git(self.state, "rm", "-f", "--", path)
        elif change == "mode-change":
            path.chmod(path.stat().st_mode | stat.S_IXUSR)
            self.env.update(GIT_CONFIG_COUNT="3", GIT_CONFIG_KEY_2="core.filemode", GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2="false")
        elif change == "type-change":
            external = self.base / "external-target"
            external.write_text("External bytes must survive.\n")
            self.extra_roots = [external]
            path.unlink()
            path.symlink_to(external)
        elif change in ("assume-unchanged", "skip-worktree"):
            self.git(self.state, "update-index", "--" + change, "--", path)
            path.write_bytes(edited)
        elif change == "stat-spoof":
            info = path.stat()
            path.write_bytes(b"X" + original[1:])
            os.utime(path, ns=(info.st_atime_ns, info.st_mtime_ns))
            self.env.update(GIT_CONFIG_COUNT="4", GIT_CONFIG_KEY_2="core.trustctime", GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2="false",
                            GIT_CONFIG_KEY_3="core.checkStat", GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_3="minimal")
        elif change == "rename-out":
            self.git(self.state, "mv", "--", path, self.state / "renamed-outside.txt")
        elif change == "rename-in":
            path = self.folder / "review/renamed-inside.txt"
            self.git(self.state, "mv", "--", self.state / "rename-source.txt", path)
        elif change == "conflict":
            relative = path.relative_to(self.state)
            oid = self.call(["git", "-C", self.state, "hash-object", "-w", "--stdin"], data="Conflict version\n").stdout.strip()
            entries = f"0 {'0' * 40}\t{relative}\n" + "".join(f"100644 {oid} {stage}\t{relative}\n" for stage in (1, 2, 3))
            self.call(["git", "-C", self.state, "update-index", "--index-info"], data=entries)
        else:
            raise AssertionError(change)
        return path

    def assert_scope_refusal(self, scenario, path, stage, extra, child_env=None, real_builder=False):
        before = self.scope_snapshot()
        result = self.build(stage, extra if real_builder else (*extra, "--spacedock", self.spy),
                            expected=None, cleanup_spy=True, child_env=child_env)
        after = self.scope_snapshot()
        builder_called = self.marker.exists()
        cleanup_called = (self.base / "cleanup-called").exists()
        if os.environ.get("DISPATCH_SCOPE_LOG"):
            with Path(os.environ["DISPATCH_SCOPE_LOG"]).open("a") as log:
                log.write(json.dumps(dict(scenario=scenario, before=before, after=after, exit=result.returncode,
                                          stdout=result.stdout, stderr=result.stderr,
                                          builder_called=builder_called, cleanup_called=cleanup_called)) + "\n")
        self.assertEqual(after, before, "refusal changed scoped or outside state")
        self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0, "dirty task scope was admitted")
        self.assertTrue(result.stderr.startswith("dispatch_stage: dispatch not built;"), result.stderr)
        self.assertIn(repr(str(path)), result.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, "")
        self.assertFalse(builder_called, "builder ran on a dirty scope")
        self.assertFalse(cleanup_called, "cleanup ran on a dirty scope")

    def test_retry_preserves_staged_record_with_worktree_at_head(self):
        stage, extra = self.scope_seed(route="retry")
        path = self.scope_dirty(self.record(), "staged-only")
        self.dirty_outside()
        self.assert_scope_refusal("reported-retry", path, stage, extra, real_builder=True)

    def test_scope_preservation_matrix(self):
        scenarios = []
        for layout in ("flat", "folder"):
            for location, route in (("task", "fresh"), ("older", "new-round"), ("report", "fresh"),
                                    ("reused", "retry"), ("reused", "advance")):
                scenarios += [(layout, route, location, state) for state in ("staged-only", "worktree-only", "equal-change", "partial")]
            scenarios += [(layout, "fresh", "report", state) for state in
                          ("staged-delete", "unstaged-delete", "both-delete", "mode-change", "type-change", "conflict",
                           "assume-unchanged", "skip-worktree", "stat-spoof", "rename-out", "rename-in")]
            scenarios += [(layout, route, "new-record", state) for route in ("fresh", "new-round", "advance")
                          for state in ("untracked", "staged-add", "staged-add-missing", "intent-to-add")]
            scenarios += [(layout, "fresh", "literal", "literal"), (layout, "fresh", "new-record", "ignored-existing"),
                          (layout, "fresh", "new-report", "untracked")]
        selected = [row for row in scenarios if not os.environ.get("DISPATCH_SCOPE_CASE")
                    or ":".join(row) == os.environ["DISPATCH_SCOPE_CASE"]]
        self.assertTrue(selected, "unknown scope matrix case")
        for layout, route, location, change in selected:
            scenario = ":".join((layout, route, location, change))
            with self.subTest(scenario=scenario):
                fixture = type(self)("test_scope_preservation_matrix")
                try:
                    fixture.setUp()
                    stage, extra = fixture.scope_seed(layout, route)
                    if location == "new-record":
                        number = 1 if route == "fresh" else 2
                        path = fixture.record(stage, number)
                        if route == "advance":
                            extra += ("--note", "next", "--symptom", "none")
                        if change == "ignored-existing":
                            ignore = fixture.state / ".gitignore"
                            ignore.write_text(f"/{path.relative_to(fixture.state)}\n")
                            fixture.git(fixture.state, "add", "--", ignore)
                            fixture.git(fixture.state, "commit", "-m", "test: ignored target")
                    else:
                        path = {"task": fixture.entity, "older": fixture.older, "report": fixture.report,
                                "reused": fixture.record(stage), "literal": fixture.literal,
                                "new-report": fixture.folder / "review/untracked/deep.txt"}[location]
                    path = fixture.scope_dirty(path, change)
                    fixture.dirty_outside()
                    fixture.assert_scope_refusal(scenario, path, stage, extra)
                finally:
                    fixture.doCleanups()

    def outside_snapshot(self):
        relative = self.outside.relative_to(self.state)
        return (self.outside.read_bytes(), self.git(self.state, "show", f":{relative}"),
                self.git(self.state, "ls-files", "--stage", "--", relative),
                (self.state / "untracked-other-task.txt").read_bytes())

                    fixture.assertTrue(changed)

                                           or path.startswith(fixture.slug + "/") for path in changed), changed)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Exercise dispatch records through the real Spacedock binary in split-root repos."""

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
import uuid

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
WRAPPER = ROOT / "scripts/dispatch_stage.py"
CHECKER = ROOT / "scripts/dispatch_records.py"
BINARY = os.environ.get("SPACEDOCK_BIN")


class DispatchStageTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="dispatch-stage-")
        self.addCleanup(temporary.cleanup)
        self.base = Path(temporary.name).resolve()
        self.repo = self.base / "code"
        self.workflow = self.repo / "docs/dev2"
        self.workflow.mkdir(parents=True)
        self.slug = "dispatch-fixture-" + uuid.uuid4().hex
        self.addCleanup(self.remove_artifacts)
        self.env = {key: value for key, value in os.environ.items()
                    if key not in ("GIT_DIR", "GIT_WORK_TREE", "GIT_INDEX_FILE", "GIT_COMMON_DIR")}
        self.env.update(GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="Dispatch Fixture", GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="Dispatch Fixture",
                        GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="fixture@example.invalid", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="fixture@example.invalid",
                        GIT_CONFIG_COUNT="2", GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0="commit.gpgsign", GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0="false",
                        GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1="core.hooksPath", GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1="/dev/null", PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE="1")
        (self.workflow / "README.md").write_bytes((ROOT / "references/sd/workflow.md").read_bytes())
        (self.repo / ".gitignore").write_text(".worktrees/\n**/.spacedock-state/\n")
        self.call(["git", "init", "--initial-branch=main", self.repo])
        self.git(self.repo, "add", "--", ".gitignore", "docs/dev2/README.md")
        self.git(self.repo, "commit", "-m", "test: workflow")
        self.state = self.workflow / ".spacedock-state"
        self.git(self.repo, "worktree", "add", "--detach", self.state)
        self.git(self.state, "checkout", "--orphan", "spacedock-state/dev2")
        self.git(self.state, "rm", "-rf", ".")
        self.entity = self.state / f"{self.slug}.md"
        self.entity.write_text("---\ntitle: Synthetic dispatch\nvariant: kc-dev-flow-2\nprofile: pilot\n"
                               "status: ideation\n---\n\n## FO alignment\n\nSurfaces: none\nVisible change: none\n")
        self.commit_task()
        self.folder = self.state / self.slug
        self.checklist = self.base / "checklist.txt"
        self.checklist.write_text("Inspect the real dispatch seam\nKeep the received second checklist line\n")
        self.notes = self.base / "notes.txt"
        self.notes.write_text(f"Package root: {ROOT}\nSend your completion message to `main`.\n"
                              "Keep this second scope-notes line verbatim.\n")
        self.spy = self.base / "spy"
        self.marker = self.base / "called"
        self.spy.write_text(f"#!{sys.executable}\nfrom pathlib import Path\nimport subprocess, sys\n"
                            f"Path({str(self.marker)!r}).write_text('called')\n"
                            f"sys.exit(subprocess.call([{BINARY!r}, *sys.argv[1:]]))\n")
        self.spy.chmod(0o755)

    def remove_artifacts(self):
        for path in Path("/tmp/spacedock-dispatch").glob(f"*{self.slug}*"):
            if path.is_file():
                path.unlink()

    def call(self, args, expected=0, child_env=None, data=None):
        result = subprocess.run(list(map(str, args)), cwd=self.base, env=child_env or self.env,
                                input=data, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
        if os.environ.get("DISPATCH_STAGE_LOG"):
            with Path(os.environ["DISPATCH_STAGE_LOG"]).open("a") as log:
                log.write(json.dumps(dict(argv=list(map(str, args)), exit=result.returncode,
                                          stdout=result.stdout, stderr=result.stderr)) + "\n")
        if expected is not None:
            self.assertEqual(result.returncode, expected, (args, result.stdout, result.stderr))
        return result

    def git(self, root, *args):
        return self.call(["git", "--literal-pathspecs", "-C", root, *args]).stdout.strip()

    def commit_task(self):
        self.git(self.state, "add", "--", self.entity.relative_to(self.state))
        self.git(self.state, "commit", "-m", "test: task")

    def set_stage(self, stage):
        self.entity.write_text(self.entity.read_text().replace("status: ideation", f"status: {stage}"))
        self.commit_task()

    def build(self, stage="ideation", extra=(), expected=0, cleanup_spy=False, child_env=None):

usage: number_guards.py [-h] {check,reserve} ...

Refuse candidates that change an applied migration or take a number another task holds, and reserve numbers per task.

check   exit 0 clean, 1 findings, 2 misconfiguration. Rules: R1 a migration present at the merge-base is
        modified or deleted; R2 the same against every 'Applied at: <env> <sha>' commit; R3 an added migration
        number is not above the base tip's highest; R4 an added migration or ADR number is not in the task's

        'profile: poc' differs from the merge-base anywhere under the migrations directory; R7 (only under
        'migrations-path: none') the candidate adds a file named NNNN_name.sql anywhere; R8 an added ADR
        number absent from the base tip is held by another live task.
        'migrations-path: none' declares that the repository has no migration files: R1 to R3 and R6 are skipped,
        the ADR rules R4, R5 and R8 still run, and a db task is no longer exit 2.
reserve prints 'Migration: NNNN' or 'ADR: NNNN' (one above the base tip and every other live task, never
        filling a gap); a task that already holds a line gets it back. One number per kind per task.
Holders: own state *.md and */index.md, plus every origin/spacedock-state/* branch fetched explicitly.
        The checked task's path is excluded on its own branch only when its state checkout has origin.
Limits: only files named NNNN_name.sql count as migrations, so meta/_journal.json and snapshots are not checked (R6 does check them);
a deploy nobody recorded as 'Applied at:' is not detected; run 'git -C <repo> fetch' first, the base tip is what is local.
Task lines are read from the task's '## Number guards' section.

--names reports skipped context checks on stderr. --strict requires --names and at least one record;
it exits 2 for a record outside task/dispatch or without an adjacent task file, after running the existing checks.
--names also refuses a live validation rerun with open F-numbered Needs decision findings until a later
committed native Captain validation resolution or Captain amendment exists (ADR 0045). It skips this predicate
for non-git snapshots; missing or ambiguous required git history exits 2.
--newest runs that scan on the file added by the latest commit that adds a file under <slug>/dispatch/, read as it
is on disk: exit 0 when it is clean or the task has no record, 1 when a name is found, 2 when git cannot read the state.
--coverage checks presence for a declared ideation, implementation or validation stage after an unfenced report:
exit 0 when not due or covered, 1 when missing, 2 for invalid input or read errors. A positive-numbered stage
record or stage message record covers repeated reports; contents and historical send timing are not checked.
Folder mode checks each stage's newest implementation/validation record, including follow-up messages;
--names checks the named record. Record number, then message number, orders the records numerically.
From the second same-stage Symptom: header, stderr prints step-back questions before dispatch. Record N >= 2
without that header gets a stderr hint; only --names --strict holds it. The first record needs no header.
"""
import argparse
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from decision_ledger import split_task, gate_entries
from delivery_gate import CANDIDATE, RECORD  # noqa: E402
from design_surfaces import added_words, AMENDMENTS_HEADING, AMENDMENT_HEADER, amendment_form, parse_amendments, alignment_owes_result, dispatched_amendments, escaped_amendment_lines, task_folder  # noqa: E402
        print(f"{file}:1: context checks not run: {notice}", file=sys.stderr)
        status = 2
    return status


def check_symptoms(files):
    missing = False
    for file in files:
        path = Path(file).resolve()
        record = DIAGNOSIS_RECORD.fullmatch(path.name)
        if path.parent.name != "dispatch" or not record:
            continue
        symptom = symptom_name(path.read_text())
        if int(record[2]) >= 2 and not symptom:
            print(f"{file}:1: no 'Symptom:' line; before first '## ' heading add "
                  "'Symptom: <failure, named the same way each time>' or 'Symptom: none'", file=sys.stderr)
            missing = True
        dispatches = [(p.name, p.read_text()) for p in path.parent.glob(f"{record[1]}-*.md")
                      if (match := DIAGNOSIS_RECORD.fullmatch(p.name)) and diagnosis_order(match) <= diagnosis_order(record)]
        group = symptom_rounds(dispatches).get((record[1], symptom), [])
        if symptom and any(number == int(record[2]) for number, _ in group) and len(group) >= 2:
            print(f'{file}:1: step back: {len(group)} {record[1]} dispatches name symptom "{symptom}"; '
                  f"before you send this one, answer: {STEP_BACK}", file=sys.stderr)
    return int(missing)


NUMBER = re.compile(r"\d+")


def named_section(text, heading):
    return 0


def main(argv=None, package=PACKAGE):
    args = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
    if args[:1] == ["--names"]:
        strict = "--strict" in args[1:]
        files = [arg for arg in args[1:] if arg != "--strict"]
        if not files:
            print(__doc__.strip())
            return 2
        status = max(check_names(files, package), check_candidates(files), check_task_facts(files), check_validation_rulings(files))
        context = check_context(files)
        symptoms = check_symptoms(files)
        return max(status, context, symptoms) if strict else status
    if "--strict" in args:
        print(__doc__.strip())
        return 2
    if args[:1] == ["--newest"] and len(args) == 3:
        return check_newest(args[1], args[2], package)
    readme = None
    if "--readme" in args:
        at = args.index("--readme")
        given, args = args[at + 1:at + 2], args[:at] + args[at + 2:]
        if not given:
            print(__doc__.strip())
            return 2
        readme = Path(given[0])
        if not readme.is_file():
            print(f"--readme {readme}: no such file")
            return 2
    if "--coverage" in args:
        return check_coverage(args, readme)
    if len(args) != 1 or args[0] in ("--names", "--newest"):
        print(__doc__.strip())
        return 2
    task = Path(args[0])
    folder = task_folder(task) if task.suffix == ".md" else task
    records = sorted((folder / "dispatch").glob("*.md"))
    if not records:
        print(f"{folder}: no dispatch records under dispatch/")
        return 1
    readme = readme or find_readme(folder)
    # see docs/adr/0048-paseo-stage-workers-complete-by-final-reply-and-hand-publication-to-fo.md
    try:
        listed = readme_extensions(readme) if readme else []
    except (OSError, UnicodeError, ValueError) as error:
        print(f"{readme}: {error}")
        return 2
    paseo = "paseo" in listed
    errors = []
    for path in records:
        text = path.read_text()
        for part, pattern in PARTS.items():
            if not pattern.search(text) and not (part == COMPLETION_PART and paseo and PASEO_COMPLETION.search(text)):
                errors.append(f"{path.name}: needs {part}")
    if readme:
        errors += extension_errors(folder, readme, package)
    names = [path.stem for path in records]
    for path in records:
        if only_points_at_records(path.read_text(), [name for name in names if name != path.stem]):
            errors.append(f"{path.name}: needs a checklist of its own, not only a reference to another dispatch record")
    for error in errors:
        print(error)
    newest = {}
    for path in records:
        record = DIAGNOSIS_RECORD.fullmatch(path.name)
        if record and diagnosis_order(record) > newest.get(record[1], ((0, 0), None))[0]:
            newest[record[1]] = (diagnosis_order(record), path)
    check_symptoms([path for _, path in newest.values()])
    if not readme:
        print(f"extensions not checked: no workflow README above {folder}")
    if not errors:
        print(f"{len(records)} dispatch record(s) complete")
    return 1 if errors else 0

# 0026. Role calls are owed on counts read from task records, and a dated call clears them whatever it says

Date: 2026-10-20

## Status

Accepted

## Context

`role_triggers.py` owed a chief-engineer call on a `- Cycle N` line under `### Feedback Cycles` and cleared a call only when its question named `Cycle 3` or `Amendment N`. Over 38 window tasks in four repositories it read 0 events in the two that record cycles in stage-report headings, and it refused 3 of the 4 calls FO had made (two worded "third repair cycle", one filed under another heading). The Captain's direction on 2026-10-20 was counts from structured records, not keywords. The measurement, the per-task table and the falsified alternatives are in the task's `## Design`. This supersedes the wording-match clause of the special-role-triggers design (PR #664), which has no ADR of its own to amend.

## Decision

**Words:** 「設計時不應該過度依賴關鍵字，而是可能要依靠犯錯字數觸發，合理嗎？」 — Captain, 2026-10-20, chat; 「先加第一個，第二個列入評估」 — Captain, 2026-10-20, chat, on the engineering-reviewer model rule and the security-reviewer evaluation; at the ideation gate, 2026-10-20, D1 「同意」, D2 「第四輪」, D3 「Ａ」, D4 「Ａ」, D5 「同意」, each as the gate question recommended.

**Options considered:**
- Chief-engineer is owed at four repair passes, read as `## Stage Report: implementation` headings minus one (chosen, D2); three passes fires one more false case (go-live-consent); a sent-back count added one case and needs a free-text verdict match that leaves 105 of 410 validation reports unreadable; same-path review rounds, holds or overrides, ADR-draft headings and cross-references added no unique true catch or false-fired
- Engineering-reviewer keeps its replacing-amendment event, one line per task, cleared by a call dated no earlier than the amendment on a model no lower than the one required, or by a dated waiver (chosen)
- Model: Fable when the frontmatter says `profile: prod` or the `Surfaces:` line lists `db`, else Opus, never lower (chosen, D4); path or secret signals were not chosen (the authority-path signal marks 31 of 38 tasks, secrets have no field)
- Review rounds, two review ids with inline findings on an open task PR, also owe chief-engineer, as a last separate slice (chosen, D1)
- The four engineering-reviewer cases no count sees stay with judgment and no `Reverses:` line is added (chosen, D3)
- ADR 0021 D1 stays: stage 1 of the evaluation reads saved reports and runs no model, stage 2 waits for its result (chosen, D5)

**Recommended:** each of D1 to D5 as the gate question stated, which the Captain accepted.

A call or a waiver counts only as a `Reviewer:` line under `## FO alignment`, and a call counts by its date and model, not by its question. Later work that changes what owes a role call reads counts from committed task records and does not match phrases.

## Consequences

FO is told once per task and role, in the line `pr_watch.py tasks` already prints, until the call is recorded. A call on another question dated after an amendment now clears it. A count cannot see an authority change, a ruling reversed in another task or a new authority surface; those stay with the Captain and FO. The thresholds are in-sample on one 38-task window judged by four observers. Reopen when a batch shows an owed case the count missed twice in the same shape, or a false fire on a task whose extra passes were phases.

Amended 2026-10-22 (Captain: 「可以」 at the ideation gate of the task `merge-ask-holds-missing-clauses`, narrowing it to this one hold; 「按建議**不算**」 on D2): `delivery_gate.py check` runs `role_triggers.py` on the task folder and stem, without `--review-rounds`, and holds the merge ask while the committed task owes a chief-engineer call (four repair passes) or an engineering-reviewer call (a replacing amendment): exit 1 adds one problem line and the script's `next:` lines, exit 2 holds with its message (「可以」). Review rounds do not hold the ask; idle still prints that call (「按建議不算」). The script reads the task as committed, so an amendment not yet state-committed is not seen and a call not yet state-committed does not clear. "Told once per task and role" above still describes the idle line; a skipped call now also refuses the merge ask until the call or a dated waiver is committed.

Amended 2026-10-25 (Captain: 「都開」 on 2026-10-23 and 「可以」 on 2026-10-25 for the task `role-triggers-owe-ce-on-review-drift`; 「全准」 at its ideation gate on 2026-10-25, accepting D1 and D2 as the gate question recommended): a review-round event is cleared only by a chief-engineer call or waiver dated no earlier than the UTC date of the newest review round, which `pr_watch.py tasks` reads from the one comment list it already fetches and passes as `--drift-date`; a call about something else made before that round no longer clears it, and no file-path test is used (D1). A call made earlier on the same date as that round still clears it. Without `--drift-date` any call or waiver clears, as before; the repair-pass event keeps its undated clear. The merge ask still does not count review rounds (D2).

Amended 2026-11-02: Astra meets the Fable floor, and chief-engineer calls need opus rank or above, for both repair-pass and review-round events. The date and waiver rules stay as recorded above; see ADR 0049 for the Captain's words and the accepted model table.

Amended 2026-11-02 (Captain: 「可以」, answering 「決定：多開「完成通知」和「挑剔使用者可用 Gemini」兩張票，先前五件事照建議，可以嗎？」 at the ideation revision of `second-round-prompts-a-step-back`; then 「照建議」, answering 「決定：五張設計進實作、Gemini 這張停在這裡，四個決定都照建議嗎？要改哪件直接說。」 at its ideation approval): two validation reports with a Material or Needs decision F bullet, or two amendments whose `Supersedes:` does not start with `none`, print the three questions at idle and merge without a hold. The counts stay separate. D1 follows this record's structured-count rule and ADR 0045's F-bullet form, accepting that 5 of 13 word-detected tasks stay silent; replacing amendments count, not every relaxation. At either count's third occurrence, D2 follows the repair/amendment merge hold and existing waiver, rather than review rounds' non-hold; D3 assigns chief-engineer because an engineering-reviewer call already clears amendments whatever its question. Its one owed line carries: is what I am solving still the outcome first asked for; can this gap be tested now, or am I waiting; what breaks if this criterion or process is deleted? The opus-rank floor applies, Astra included. A call or waiver dated no earlier than the third amendment clears that event, reusing the drift-date rule; any qualifying call or waiver clears failed validations, reusing the undated repair rule. A fourth occurrence owes no second call; engineering-reviewer's amendment event stays separate. At count two, questions repeat on each run without an answer record; at three or more, a cleared event prints no reminder.

Amended 2026-11-02 (Captain: 「照建議」, answering 「決定：四件事都照建議嗎？要改哪件直接說。」 after FO proposed 「修這兩個 bug，在原本的票裡修」, recorded in `second-round-prompts-a-step-back` Captain amendment 1): each count reaches its own reminder threshold independently. A cleared event at three or more does not suppress the other event's second-occurrence reminder. Suppress a duplicate reminder only when an emitted owed-call line already carries the three questions; all model, date, waiver and merge-hold rules above remain.

Amended 2026-11-03 (Captain: 「可以」, answering 「決定：七張設計照建議進實作，但驗收到期提醒的 D7 改成『在 kc-journey-map 登記 journey-progress/v1，預算放寬為兩個 PR，kc-journey-map 那個先合併』，可以嗎？」 at the ideation gate of `diagnosis-rounds-count-toward-step-back`, accepting its D1 and D2 as recommended): dispatch records count diagnosis rounds by stage and normalized `Symptom:` header, trimming and collapsing spaces and casefolding; values starting with `none`, fenced lines and body lines do not count. At round two, `dispatch_records.py` prints the three step-back questions on stderr before each dispatch, following ADR 0027's placement at the write; folder mode checks each stage's highest-numbered record, and `--names` counts only through the named record. A record numbered two or higher without the header gets a stderr hint; only `--names --strict` holds it (D1). Idle and merge read committed records: round two advises without a hold, round three owes chief-engineer and holds the merge ask (D2). An opus-rank-or-above call or waiver under `## FO alignment`, dated no earlier than the third record's first `Dispatched:` date, clears that symptom's later rounds too; without that date any qualifying call or waiver clears. Other event families remain independent; an owed line carrying the questions suppresses duplicate reminders. With the replay's symptom name, measured added words are 48 per dispatch reminder, 21 per missing-header hint, 47 at idle/merge round two and 74 at round three; a clean dispatch, startup, after archive and the workflow template add zero. The workflow word budget is unchanged. Renamed symptoms and multiple browser runs inside one dispatch remain outside the count.

Clarified 2026-11-03 (Captain: 「照你建議」, answering 「決定：B 照原設計修，讓追加指示紀錄也算進同症狀的輪數嗎？」, Captain amendment 1 of `diagnosis-rounds-count-toward-step-back`, superseding no criterion): a supported `<stage>-N-message-M.md` follow-up is a dispatch round on its own symptom, as the approved design states. Both disk and committed-state readers count it; record number, then message number, gives numeric order, with the plain record before its messages. The third counted record dates clearing whether it is plain or a follow-up.

# 0026. Role calls are owed on counts read from task records, and a dated call clears them whatever it says

Date: 2026-10-20

## Status

Accepted

## Context

`role_triggers.py` owed a chief-engineer call on a `- Cycle N` line under `### Feedback Cycles` and cleared a call only when its question named `Cycle 3` or `Amendment N`. Over 38 window tasks in four repositories it read 0 events in the two that record cycles in stage-report headings, and it refused 3 of the 4 calls FO had made (two worded "third repair cycle", one filed under another heading). The Captain's direction on 2026-10-20 was counts from structured records, not keywords. The measurement, the per-task table and the falsified alternatives are in the task's `## Design`. This supersedes the wording-match clause of the special-role-triggers design (PR #664), which has no ADR of its own to amend.

## Decision

**Words:** 「設計時不應該過度依賴關鍵字，而是可能要依靠犯錯字數觸發，合理嗎？」 — Captain, 2026-10-20, chat; 「先加第一個，第二個列入評估」 — Captain, 2026-10-20, chat, on the engineering-reviewer model rule and the security-reviewer evaluation; at the ideation gate, 2026-10-20, D1 「同意」, D2 「第四輪」, D3 「Ａ」, D4 「Ａ」, D5 「同意」, each as the gate question recommended.

**Options considered:**
- Chief-engineer is owed at four repair passes, read as `## Stage Report: implementation` headings minus one (chosen, D2); three passes fires one more false case (go-live-consent); a sent-back count added one case and needs a free-text verdict match that leaves 105 of 410 validation reports unreadable; same-path review rounds, holds or overrides, ADR-draft headings and cross-references added no unique true catch or false-fired
- Engineering-reviewer keeps its replacing-amendment event, one line per task, cleared by a call dated no earlier than the amendment on a model no lower than the one required, or by a dated waiver (chosen)
- Model: Fable when the frontmatter says `profile: prod` or the `Surfaces:` line lists `db`, else Opus, never lower (chosen, D4); path or secret signals were not chosen (the authority-path signal marks 31 of 38 tasks, secrets have no field)
- Review rounds, two review ids with inline findings on an open task PR, also owe chief-engineer, as a last separate slice (chosen, D1)
- The four engineering-reviewer cases no count sees stay with judgment and no `Reverses:` line is added (chosen, D3)
- ADR 0021 D1 stays: stage 1 of the evaluation reads saved reports and runs no model, stage 2 waits for its result (chosen, D5)

**Recommended:** each of D1 to D5 as the gate question stated, which the Captain accepted.

A call or a waiver counts only as a `Reviewer:` line under `## FO alignment`, and a call counts by its date and model, not by its question. Later work that changes what owes a role call reads counts from committed task records and does not match phrases.

## Consequences

FO is told once per task and role, in the line `pr_watch.py tasks` already prints, until the call is recorded. A call on another question dated after an amendment now clears it. A count cannot see an authority change, a ruling reversed in another task or a new authority surface; those stay with the Captain and FO. The thresholds are in-sample on one 38-task window judged by four observers. Reopen when a batch shows an owed case the count missed twice in the same shape, or a false fire on a task whose extra passes were phases.

Amended 2026-10-22 (Captain: 「可以」 at the ideation gate of the task `merge-ask-holds-missing-clauses`, narrowing it to this one hold; 「按建議**不算**」 on D2): `delivery_gate.py check` runs `role_triggers.py` on the task folder and stem, without `--review-rounds`, and holds the merge ask while the committed task owes a chief-engineer call (four repair passes) or an engineering-reviewer call (a replacing amendment): exit 1 adds one problem line and the script's `next:` lines, exit 2 holds with its message (「可以」). Review rounds do not hold the ask; idle still prints that call (「按建議不算」). The script reads the task as committed, so an amendment not yet state-committed is not seen and a call not yet state-committed does not clear. "Told once per task and role" above still describes the idle line; a skipped call now also refuses the merge ask until the call or a dated waiver is committed.

Amended 2026-10-25 (Captain: 「都開」 on 2026-10-23 and 「可以」 on 2026-10-25 for the task `role-triggers-owe-ce-on-review-drift`; 「全准」 at its ideation gate on 2026-10-25, accepting D1 and D2 as the gate question recommended): a review-round event is cleared only by a chief-engineer call or waiver dated no earlier than the UTC date of the newest review round, which `pr_watch.py tasks` reads from the one comment list it already fetches and passes as `--drift-date`; a call about something else made before that round no longer clears it, and no file-path test is used (D1). A call made earlier on the same date as that round still clears it. Without `--drift-date` any call or waiver clears, as before; the repair-pass event keeps its undated clear. The merge ask still does not count review rounds (D2).

Amended 2026-11-02: Astra meets the Fable floor, and chief-engineer calls need opus rank or above, for both repair-pass and review-round events. The date and waiver rules stay as recorded above; see ADR 0049 for the Captain's words and the accepted model table.

Amended 2026-11-02 (Captain: 「可以」, answering 「決定：多開「完成通知」和「挑剔使用者可用 Gemini」兩張票，先前五件事照建議，可以嗎？」 at the ideation revision of `second-round-prompts-a-step-back`; then 「照建議」, answering 「決定：五張設計進實作、Gemini 這張停在這裡，四個決定都照建議嗎？要改哪件直接說。」 at its ideation approval): two validation reports with a Material or Needs decision F bullet, or two amendments whose `Supersedes:` does not start with `none`, print the three questions at idle and merge without a hold. A cleared event at three or more does not suppress the other event's second-occurrence reminder. Suppress a duplicate reminder only when an emitted owed-call line already carries the three questions; all model, date, waiver and merge-hold rules above remain.

Amended 2026-11-03 (Captain: 「可以」, answering 「決定：七張設計照建議進實作，但驗收到期提醒的 D7 改成『在 kc-journey-map 登記 journey-progress/v1，預算放寬為兩個 PR，kc-journey-map 那個先合併』，可以嗎？」 at the ideation gate of `diagnosis-rounds-count-toward-step-back`, accepting its D1 and D2 as recommended): dispatch records count diagnosis rounds by stage and normalized `Symptom:` header, trimming and collapsing spaces and casefolding; values starting with `none`, fenced lines and body lines do not count. At round two, `dispatch_records.py` prints the three step-back questions on stderr before each dispatch, following ADR 0027's placement at the write; folder mode checks each stage's highest-numbered record, and `--names` counts only through the named record. A record numbered two or higher without the header gets a stderr hint; only `--names --strict` holds it (D1). Idle and merge read committed records: round two advises without a hold, round three owes chief-engineer and holds the merge ask (D2). An opus-rank-or-above call or waiver under `## FO alignment`, dated no earlier than the third record's first `Dispatched:` date, clears that symptom's later rounds too; without that date any qualifying call or waiver clears. A dispatch built with `dispatch build --stamp` leaves <task>/dispatch/<stage>-<cycle>.md written from the same checklist, scope notes, model and SHA it sends, so the record no longer depends on FO remembering it.

## Scope

- Source: the Captain 「開」 (chat, 2026-11-06), answering 「要開這 4 張嗎？」 after fo-feedback round 005 (.notes/fo-feedback/round-005.md, closed 2026-11-06).
- Bite: kc-paseo-plugins reconstructed every dispatch record of batch r1b-polish-1 after the fact (_archive/project-env-rate-limit-cause/dispatch/ideation-1.md: "Reconstructed by FO on 2026-11-06, after the dispatch"; FO read 2026-11-06); qnow sent a follow-up addendum with no record (observer); the kc-plugin FO wrote one message record late and omitted required lines in batches 14 and 15 (observer reports).
- Upstream first: Spacedock dispatch build --stamp (Spacedock is not the Captain's repository: a change there is an upstream issue, so the dev2 side may be a package wrapper); kc-dev-flow-2 dispatch_records.py, which checks the record.
- Non-goals: follow-up messages to a running worker (a separate record kind).

## Budget
- One package PR; the workflow word budget does not rise unless the design names a raise for the Captain.

## Stop condition
- A stamped dispatch leaves a record that dispatch_records.py accepts without FO writing it, or the design names why Spacedock cannot and what the package does instead.

## FO alignment

Alignment: needed at ideation; the design choice is his to accept.
Result: aligned at backlog: Batch 17 backlog sitting, the Captain 「核准（建議）」 (host question dialog, 2026-11-07), answering 「決定：第 17 批這五張（Paseo 瀏覽器當工人驗收的預設、決策紀錄檢查分清驗證取代與指向依據、派工時自動寫派工紀錄、沒給範圍時設計檢查說沒跑、觀察者列出沒有合併提問紀錄的合併）都用 Pilot，照各自寫下的範圍、預算與停止條件進入構想嗎？建議核准。要改哪張直接說。」, approved the outcome and bounds in this file; the design choice the Alignment line names stays his at the ideation gate.
Surfaces: none
Visible change: none
Release review: not needed: workflow maintenance, on no journey map.

## Design

### Chain check

Read 2026-11-07 at the pins named here.

- **Spacedock** (`spacedock-dev/spacedock` origin/main 324c61588, and tag v0.27.2, the installed and CI-pinned binary): `dispatch build --stamp` (`runStamp` in `internal/dispatch/stamp.go`) stamps `started`/`worktree`, makes one path-scoped state commit `dispatch: <slug> entering <stage>`, publishes it and creates the worktree; `runBuildFields` in `build.go` then writes only `/tmp/spacedock-dispatch/<name>.md`. Nothing writes `<task>/dispatch/`. Mods have four hook points only (`git grep -hoE '## Hook: [a-z-]+'`: startup, merge, idle, shutdown); none runs at dispatch. The build also cannot know the record's `Model:` line: on Claude its envelope `model` is the Agent enum (`opus`), and a Paseo dispatch's model and `Roster:` come from `model_roster.py`, which Spacedock does not read.
- **The seam the design uses:** `entityCommitPaths` puts the task's companion folder `<slug>/` into the stamp commit (`git add -A -- <slug>.md <slug>/`). Probe on 0.27.2 (`/tmp/stamp-probe.3Byi`, split-root fixture with this workflow's README): an uncommitted `probe/dispatch/ideation-1.md` was committed by `dispatch: probe entering ideation`; on a second build for the same stage, with `started` already set, `ideation-2.md` alone was committed by the same subject. `spacedock state commit probe` committed an uncommitted `implementation-1.md` as `state: update probe`, which covers `--advance`, where `--stamp` is refused.
- **kc-dev-flow-2** (origin/main 139feeaee, 0.35.0): `dispatch_records.py` checks a record and writes none; `replay_dispatch.py` wraps `dispatch build` for replays and copies the dispatch file into its run folder, not a record. `git grep 'dispatch build'` finds no other writer.
- **Adopters** (subspace-relay, subspace-web, qnow, `origin/HEAD`, read-only `git grep -lE 'dispatch build|dispatch_records|/dispatch/[a-z]+-'`): their synced `docs/dev2*/README.md`, plus qnow history notes; no wrapper and no record writer.

So Spacedock cannot write the record without an upstream change in a repository the Captain does not own, and it would still lack the model line. The package wraps the build instead.

### PRFAQ

**kc-dev-flow-2 records every worker dispatch as it builds it.** FO now builds a worker dispatch with one package script. The script writes `<task>/dispatch/<stage>-<cycle>.md` from the same checklist and scope-notes files it hands to `spacedock dispatch build --stamp`, adds the model and the workflow checkout's SHA, runs both `dispatch_records.py` checks, and only then builds. The stamp's own state commit carries the record, so a record cannot be missing, written after the fact, or different from what the worker received.

- *What does FO still write?* The checklist and the scope notes, as today, and the model, roster, candidate and symptom values as flags. The script writes the header, the sections and the cycle number.
- *What if a part is missing?* The script removes the file it wrote, prints the checker's lines, and builds nothing. Its message starts `dispatch_stage: dispatch not built;`, so FO does not mistake it for a `dispatch build` failure that allows break-glass dispatch.
- *What if the build fails?* Spacedock's stderr and exit code pass through unchanged. If the record was not committed, the script removes it; an identical immediate rerun reuses the committed number instead of minting a new one.
- *Follow-up messages to a live worker?* Not covered: FO still saves those by hand.
- *Acceptance evidence:* a test against the CI-pinned Spacedock 0.27.2 binary (AC-1 to AC-6), and the README and pinned tests (AC-7).

### Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  G[FO: task status equals the stage] --> W["dispatch_stage.py: build flags, --model, optional --roster / --candidate / --symptom"]
  W --> U{flag values valid?}
  U -- no --> U2[usage error, exit 2, no file written]
  U -- yes --> N{"newest record of this stage identical and added by the state HEAD commit?"}
  N -- yes --> K[reuse its number, write nothing]
  N -- no --> R["write task/dispatch/stage-N.md, N = newest + 1"]
  K --> C
  R --> C{"dispatch_records.py folder check and --names --strict"}
  C -- nonzero --> X["remove the file it wrote, print the checker lines, exit 1, no build"]
  C -- zero --> A{--advance?}
  A -- no --> S[spacedock dispatch build --stamp]
  A -- yes --> V[spacedock dispatch build --advance]
  S -- nonzero --> F["remove the record if uncommitted; pass Spacedock stderr and exit code"]
  V -- nonzero --> F
  S -- zero --> E["stamp commit carries the record; envelope JSON on stdout"]
  V -- zero --> SC{spacedock state commit slug}
```

**AC-1** A stamped dispatch leaves a record `dispatch_records.py` accepts, committed by the stamp. **AC-2** The record holds what the worker receives. Evidence: the same test asserts every nonblank line of the checklist and scope-notes files appears in the record's matching section and in the file at `dispatch_file_path`. Falsifier: writing the record from a copy with one scope-notes line dropped fails it.

**AC-3** An incomplete record builds nothing and leaves nothing. Evidence: a scope-notes file without `Package root:` gives exit 1, a first stderr line starting `dispatch_stage: dispatch not built;` followed by the checker's part line, no file under `<task>/dispatch/`, the state checkout's HEAD and the task file unchanged, and no call to a fake `--spacedock` that writes a marker file when run. **AC-4** A validation dispatch without a candidate is held before the build. Evidence: `--stage validation` without `--candidate` exits 1 with `dispatch_records.py`'s "no 'Candidate: <40-hex head>' line" text and leaves no file; `--candidate abc` exits 2 before writing. Falsifier: ignoring the checker's exit code lets the fake build run.

**AC-5** A failed or repeated build leaves no phantom record. Evidence: (a) a task at `status: backlog` dispatched with `--stage ideation`: Spacedock's stderr line starting `dispatch build --stamp:` and its exit code 1 pass through, and no `ideation-1.md` remains; (b) right after a successful `ideation-1`, an identical rerun exits 0 and adds no `ideation-2.md`, while the same rerun after one unrelated state commit adds `ideation-2.md`; (c) a rerun with one changed checklist line adds `ideation-2.md`, committed by the stamp. Falsifiers: without the removal (a) leaves a file; without the identical-reuse rule the first rerun of (b) adds `ideation-2.md`; reusing on bytes alone makes the second rerun of (b) add none.

**AC-6** A reuse-advance dispatch is recorded and committed. ## Design

### Chain check

Read 2026-11-07 at the pins named here.

- **Spacedock** (`spacedock-dev/spacedock` origin/main 324c61588, and tag v0.27.2, the installed and CI-pinned binary): `dispatch build --stamp` (`runStamp` in `internal/dispatch/stamp.go`) stamps `started`/`worktree`, makes one path-scoped state commit `dispatch: <slug> entering <stage>`, publishes it and creates the worktree; `runBuildFields` in `build.go` then writes only `/tmp/spacedock-dispatch/<name>.md`. Nothing writes `<task>/dispatch/`. Mods have four hook points only (`git grep -hoE '## Hook: [a-z-]+'`: startup, merge, idle, shutdown); none runs at dispatch. The build also cannot know the record's `Model:` line: on Claude its envelope `model` is the Agent enum (`opus`), and a Paseo dispatch's model and `Roster:` come from `model_roster.py`, which Spacedock does not read.
- **The seam the design uses:** `entityCommitPaths` puts the task's companion folder `<slug>/` into the stamp commit (`git add -A -- <slug>.md <slug>/`). Probe on 0.27.2 (`/tmp/stamp-probe.3Byi`, split-root fixture with this workflow's README): an uncommitted `probe/dispatch/ideation-1.md` was committed by `dispatch: probe entering ideation`; on a second build for the same stage, with `started` already set, `ideation-2.md` alone was committed by the same subject. `spacedock state commit probe` committed an uncommitted `implementation-1.md` as `state: update probe`, which covers `--advance`, where `--stamp` is refused.
- **kc-dev-flow-2** (origin/main 139feeaee, 0.35.0): `dispatch_records.py` checks a record and writes none; `replay_dispatch.py` wraps `dispatch build` for replays and copies the dispatch file into its run folder, not a record. `git grep 'dispatch build'` finds no other writer.
- **Adopters** (subspace-relay, subspace-web, qnow, `origin/HEAD`, read-only `git grep -lE 'dispatch build|dispatch_records|/dispatch/[a-z]+-'`): their synced `docs/dev2*/README.md`, plus qnow history notes; no wrapper and no record writer.

So Spacedock cannot write the record without an upstream change in a repository the Captain does not own, and it would still lack the model line. The package wraps the build instead.

### PRFAQ

**kc-dev-flow-2 records every worker dispatch as it builds it.** FO now builds a worker dispatch with one package script. The script writes `<task>/dispatch/<stage>-<cycle>.md` from the same checklist and scope-notes files it hands to `spacedock dispatch build --stamp`, adds the model and the workflow checkout's SHA, runs both `dispatch_records.py` checks, and only then builds. The stamp's own state commit carries the record, so a record cannot be missing, written after the fact, or different from what the worker received.

- *What does FO still write?* The checklist and the scope notes, as today, and the model, roster, candidate and symptom values as flags. The script writes the header, the sections and the cycle number.
- *What if a part is missing?* The script removes the file it wrote, prints the checker's lines, and builds nothing. Its message starts `dispatch_stage: dispatch not built;`, so FO does not mistake it for a `dispatch build` failure that allows break-glass dispatch.
- *What if the build fails?* Spacedock's stderr and exit code pass through unchanged. If the record was not committed, the script removes it; an identical immediate rerun reuses the committed number instead of minting a new one.
- *Follow-up messages to a live worker?* Not covered: FO still saves those by hand.
- *Acceptance evidence:* a test against the CI-pinned Spacedock 0.27.2 binary (AC-1 to AC-6), and the README and pinned tests (AC-7).

### Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  G[FO: task status equals the stage] --> W["dispatch_stage.py: build flags, --model, optional --roster / --candidate / --symptom"]
  W --> U{flag values valid?}
  U -- no --> U2[usage error, exit 2, no file written]
  U -- yes --> N{"newest record of this stage identical and added by the state HEAD commit?"}
  N -- yes --> K[reuse its number, write nothing]
  N -- no --> R["write task/dispatch/stage-N.md, N = newest + 1"]
  K --> C
  R --> C{"dispatch_records.py folder check and --names --strict"}
  C -- nonzero --> X["remove the file it wrote, print the checker lines, exit 1, no build"]
  C -- zero --> A{--advance?}
  A -- no --> S[spacedock dispatch build --stamp]
  A -- yes --> V[spacedock dispatch build --advance]
  S -- nonzero --> F["remove the record if uncommitted; pass Spacedock stderr and exit code"]
  V -- nonzero --> F
  S -- zero --> E["stamp commit carries the record; envelope JSON on stdout"]
  V -- zero --> SC{spacedock state commit slug}
  SC -- nonzero --> F2["exit 1, envelope withheld, record left for an identical rerun"]
  SC -- zero --> E
  E --> P["FO spawns the worker from the envelope (Agent or Paseo create_agent)"]
```

### Existing-code check

Completeness: `dispatch build --stamp` works through the journey and writes no record; `dispatch_records.py` works as a checker; no record writer exists (two bounded searches: the Spacedock `## Hook:` and `dispatch/<stage>` greps, and the package and adopter `dispatch build` greps above; excluded: `_archive/` evidence copies). Need: the Scope bite, three sessions with records written late, reconstructed or short of required lines. The design adds one script and reuses `dispatch_records.py`'s checks unchanged, and `task_folder` from `design_surfaces.py`.

### What changes

One package PR:

- `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/dispatch_stage.py` (new). Arguments: `--workflow-dir`, `--entity-path`, `--stage`, `--checklist-file`, `--scope-notes-file`, optional `--feedback-context-file`/`--feedback-reflow`/`--advance` passed through, `--model TEXT` (required), `--roster TEXT`, `--candidate SHA` (repeatable, 40 hex or exit 2), `--symptom TEXT`, `--spacedock BIN` (default `$SPACEDOCK_BIN`, then `spacedock`).
  - Writes `# <stage>-<N>`, `Dispatched: <git -C workflow-dir rev-parse HEAD> (workflow checkout)`, `Model:`, then the given `Roster:`, `Candidate:` and `Symptom:` lines, `## Checklist` with the checklist file, `## Scope notes` with the scope-notes file. It never edits either file's text: an omitted `Package root:` or completion line is held by the checker, before any build.
  - N: let M be the highest `<stage>-<M>.md` committed at the state checkout's HEAD (message records excluded). N = M, writing nothing, only when that file's bytes equal what would be written and the state checkout's HEAD commit is the one that added it (an immediate retry after a sync or assembly failure); otherwise N = M + 1, 1 when none, overwriting an uncommitted file at N. Any state commit in between makes an identical dispatch a new record, so `role_triggers.py` still counts a repeated round.
  - `--note TEXT` appends `, TEXT` inside the `Dispatched:` parentheses, for the README version and batch annotations FO writes today.
  - Runs `dispatch_records.py <task folder>` and `--names --strict <record>` as subprocesses with the same Python; on success it prints nothing of theirs.
  - Without `--advance`, runs `<spacedock> dispatch build --stamp` with the build flags; with it, `dispatch build --advance` and then `<spacedock> state commit <slug> --workflow-dir <dir>`. Stdout is the build's envelope.
- `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/test_dispatch_stage.py` (new): split-root git fixtures with the README from `references/sd/workflow.md`, run against `$SPACEDOCK_BIN`; exits nonzero naming `SPACEDOCK_BIN` when it is unset, so CI cannot pass it by skipping.
- `.github/workflows/kc-dev-flow-2-tests.yml`: one step after "Install pinned Spacedock", `SPACEDOCK_BIN="$HOME/.local/bin/spacedock" python3 kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/test_dispatch_stage.py`. Cost per PR: not measured.

**AC-1** A stamped dispatch leaves a record `dispatch_records.py` accepts, committed by the stamp.
